6.71.m: The sages said: / Live long, O virtuous Sūta, whose very nature is exceedingly compassionate! / A wonderful dialogue that took place between Nārada and the Lord has indeed been related by you.
What sort of greatness of the Lord's name was heard by the great-souled Nārada? / Tell it, O preceptor, to us who listen with faith!
Sūta said: / Listen, all you sages! I shall relate an ancient event, / hearing which, O best of the twice-born, devotion to Kṛṣṇa increases.
Once Nārada, wishing to see his father, fully collected in mind, / went to the peak of Meru, attended by Siddhas and Cāraṇas.
Having bowed down there to the seated god Brahmā, the lord of the worlds, / Nārada, the best of sages, spoke to him, O twice-born.
Nārada said: / Tell me, O Lord, ruler of the universe, how much power this name has! / And what is the greatness of the name of the imperishable, great-souled one?
This one who is manifestly the ruler of the universe, this Nārāyaṇa, Hari, / the supreme self, Hṛṣīkeśa, who accompanies all living beings—
deluded by māyā, all foolish men in this worthless Kali age / do not know the blessed Lord, Adhokṣaja.
Brahmā said: / In this Kali [age] in particular, devotion is to be practiced duly, preceded by reciting the name; / you ought to hear that, my child.
Remembering victorious Viṣṇu with effort destroys sins / and is seen as the purifier of other unstated sins.
Realizing then that everything is false, reciting and murmuring the name of Hari, / freed from all sins, one goes to the supreme abode of Viṣṇu.
Those men who constantly utter the two syllables "Ha-ri", / merely by its recitation they are liberated; of this there is no doubt.
The continuous remembrance of Kṛṣṇa is supreme above all expiations. / Remembering him in the morning, at night, in the evening, and at midday,
a man attains Nārāyaṇa and the immediate destruction of sins. / When a man remembers Viṣṇu, all afflictions are destroyed;
he goes to liberation, and the attainment of heaven comes from praising that Viṣṇu. / One whose mind is fixed on Vāsudeva in muttering prayers, oblations, worship, and the like—
one should know that to be imperishable as long as there are fourteen Indras. / Where is going to the vault of heaven, which is characterized by returning [to samsara],
and where is the muttering of [the name of] Vāsudeva, the unsurpassed seed of liberation? / That mouth is the supreme holy ford where, forming an eddy,
the eastern Sarasvatī shines forth as "Reverence to Nārāyaṇa!" / Therefore, from remembering Viṣṇu day and night, the highest of men,
his Kali-evils destroyed, does not go to hell, O son. / Truth, truth, again truth has been spoken by me, O you of good vows!
Merely by the utterance of the name, one is freed from great sin. / Murmuring again and again, "Rāma, Rāma, Rāma, Rāma,"
even a cāṇḍāla becomes purified in soul; of this there is no doubt. / Kurukṣetra, and likewise Kāśī, Gayā, and Dvārikā—
all holy places have been visited by him merely by the utterance of the name. / Or whoever murmurs or recites, "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa,"
having abandoned this world, rejoices in the presence of Viṣṇu. / Joyfully murmuring and reciting "Nṛsiṃha" constantly, O twice-born,
a man who is a devotee of the Lord is freed from great sin in the Kali age. / What one obtains by meditating in the Kṛta age, sacrificing with offerings in the Tretā, and worshiping in the Dvāpara,
that one obtains in the Kali age by loudly chanting [the name of] Keśava. / Knowing this and immersed in Keśava, the Soul of the universe,
those whose sins are completely worn away go to the supreme abode of Viṣṇu. / Matsya, Kūrma, Varāha, and Nṛsiṃha, as well as Vāmana,
Rāma, [Paraśu]rāma, and Kṛṣṇa, and then Buddha and Kalki are recalled. / These ten incarnations are celebrated on earth;
by their names alone, even a killer of a brāhmaṇa is always purified. / Reciting, murmuring, and meditating on the name of Viṣṇu in the morning, anyway,
one is freed; there is no doubt here; he indeed becomes Nārāyaṇa. / Sūta said: / Having heard this, Nārada went into the greatest astonishment.
He said to his father there: What was said, O best of gods? / There are gods by the thousands, and there are Rudras by the thousands;
the ancestors exist by the hundreds, and likewise Yakṣas and Kinnaras, / Bhūtas, Pretas, Piśācas, and whatever other divine origins there are.
Neither has the greatness of their names been heard or seen / like that greatness of the name of glorious Viṣṇu which was heard by me,
by whose name alone one is freed; of this there is no doubt. / What need is there, O Lord, of performing pilgrimages to holy places, or wandering the earth,
when by hearing the greatness of his name one can attain liberation? / That mouth is indeed a great holy ford; that mouth is a sacred field,
in whose mouth is "Rāma, Rāma"; that mouth yields all desires. / What are his names, and how many are his powers, O you of good vows?
Tell me all that in detail, O grandfather. / Brahmā said: / This Viṣṇu is all-pervading, always the supreme self, eternal,
without beginning or end, glorious, the self of beings, the source of beings. / May this Viṣṇu, from whom I was born, always protect [us]!
He is the Death of Time, and he is my elder. / The imperishable, lotus-eyed, wise, immutable Person,
Viṣṇu who always reclines on Śeṣa, thousand-headed, the great master, / identical with all beings, visibly the universal form, Janārdana,
this Viṣṇu, the enemy of Kaiṭabha, the creator, the god, the lord of the universe. / I do not know his name or lineage, O bull among men.
Though I proclaim the Veda, O dear child, I am not one who knows [him fully] at any time. / Therefore go, O divine sage, to where the Sovereign of the universe resides.
And he, O best of sages, will tell you the entire truth. / He alone is the glorious Person, always the master of Kailāsa,
the best of all devotees of Viṣṇu, higher than the highest, / five-faced, the beloved of Umā, the remover of all sorrow,
Viśveśvara, Viśvanātha, always affectionate toward his devotees. / Go there, O best of gods; he will tell you all that.
Having heard his father's words, he set out to go there, / toward the abode on Kailāsa, to understand the greatness of the name.
Where the god Viśveśvara, bestower of prosperity, always resides, / Nārada saw there that god worshipped by the celestials,
seated on the peak of Kailāsa, god of gods, teacher of the universe, / five-faced, ten-armed, three-eyed, holding a trident,
bearing a skull, with a skull-topped staff, fierce, carrying a trident and sword, / holding the Pināka bow, dreadful, granting boons, riding a bull,
his body covered in ashes, richly adorned with serpents, with the moon as his crest, / resembling a dark raincloud, with the brilliance of ten million suns.
[Nārada], falling prostrate with eight limbs like a staff, [bowed] to the lord of gods sporting there. / Seeing him, Mahādeva, his eyes opened wide in wonder,
foremost and best among Vaiṣṇavas, said to the best of brāhmaṇas: / “Why have you come here? Speak, O best of divine sages.”
Nārada said: / “At one time I went to the presence of Brahmā. / There, O god, the supreme glorification of Viṣṇu was heard by me.
It was related there before me by Brahmā, O best of gods. / However much power this name has, that was heard from Brahmā’s mouth.
There the thousand names of Viṣṇu were asked about by me previously. / Then I was told by Brahmā: ‘I do not know, O Nārada.
This Mahārudra knows; he will tell it all.’ / Experiencing great astonishment, I have indeed come into your presence.
In this terrible Kali yuga, men are short-lived, / constantly intent on unrighteousness, and not steadfast in the name.
Likewise brāhmaṇas are hypocrites, always turned away from dharmas, / devoid of the twilight prayers, fallen from vows, wicked, and filthy in appearance.
As are the brāhmaṇas, so are the kṣatriyas, and the vaiśyas again and again; / likewise the śūdras and other men are not devoted to the Lord.
Śūdras and those outside the twice-born classes in the Kali [age], O Lord Viśveśvara, / do not know dharma and adharma, nor what is beneficial or unbeneficial.
Knowing this, O master, I have indeed come into your presence. / Furthermore, the glorification of the name was heard indeed from Brahmā’s mouth.
You are the god of all gods; you are always my protector, / the enemy of Tripura, the soul of the universe, and repeatedly the creator.
Speak graciously of the thousand names of Viṣṇu, / which produce good fortune for men and always engender supreme devotion,
bestowing the state of Brahman on brāhmaṇas, granting victory to kṣatriyas, / always giving wealth to vaiśyas, and bestowing happiness on śūdras.
Therefore I wish to hear it from your presence, O Maheśvara. / You are always capable of helping devotees towards Keśava.
Tell it by your grace, O one of good vows, if it is not a secret. / It is supremely pure and always contains all holy places.
Therefore I indeed wish to hear. Speak, O Lord Viśveśvara.” / Hearing Nārada’s words, his eyes wide with wonder,
his hair then stood on end as he remembered the names of Viṣṇu. / Īśvara said: / “O brāhmaṇa, this is a supreme secret: the thousand names of Viṣṇu.
Hearing this, O dear child, a person will never meet misfortune. / Once, as time passed, Pārvatī said to me:
Pārvatī said: / ‘O Lord of Kailāsa, tell me truly: / What do you repeat in prayer, O lord of gods, absorbed in supreme sovereignty?
Why is your body always smeared with ashes? Why are you always clad in an animal skin? / Why do you wear matted locks? Speak, O Lord Viśveśvara!
You are the god of all gods; you are the teacher of all rites; / you are my husband, O ruler of the universe, Lord of the Universe, lord of the world.’
Mahādeva said: / “When I was thus questioned again and again by Pārvatī, O brāhmaṇa, / everything was then explained by me, especially before her.
Listen, O Nārada, I will tell what was spoken to Pārvatī, / by which the Lord becomes pleased and grants liberation, without a doubt.
He is truly my direct father and always my kinsman; / I am always his devotee, and he is always my lord.
That I will declare completely; listen as I speak.” / Sūta said: / Having spoken thus to Nārada, he recited it, O twice-born,
the thousand names of Viṣṇu that were previously spoken to Umā, / which were obtained by Nārada from Maheśa at Kailāsa.
Once, by the course of destiny, he came from Kailāsa / to the extremely wondrous holy place named the Naimiṣa forest.
Seeing that best of sages, all the sages residing there / paid worship especially to the great-souled Nārada.
Knowing that Nārada had arrived, their eyes wide with wonder, / those Vaiṣṇava best of twice-born showered him with flowers.
Having offered water for the feet, arghya, and then waved lights, / and offered fruits and roots, they fell like a staff upon the ground.
And they said: “We have achieved our purpose in this region, O great sage! / Vision of you has come to pass—pure and destroying sins.
And by your grace, O lord of gods, the Purāṇas have been heard. / O holy one, by what means can destruction of all sins occur?

Without gifts, without austerities, without pilgrimages, austerities, and sacrifices, / without donations, without meditations, without restraint of the senses, / and without collections of scriptures, how is liberation attained?”
Nārada said: / Having bowed down to Mahādeva, the beloved of Umā, / the god of gods, teacher of the universe seated on Kailāsa’s peak, [she] asked:
Pārvatī said: / ‘O Lord, you are the supreme god, omniscient, worshipped by all. / Truly you are worshipped by the gods, even by Indra, Sūrya, and the rest.
Having worshipped you, the boon-giver, all attain their desired perfection. / You are free from birth and death, self-born, all-powerful.
What do you always meditate upon, O Master, clad in the directions, destroyer of Madana? / Why do you practice austerities, matted-haired and gray with ashes?
Or what do you repeat in prayer, O lord of gods? Indeed, great curiosity is mine. / If I am to be favored by you, tell that excellent vow in truth.’
Mahādeva said: / ‘This has not been told to anyone; this must be kept secret by me. / Yet I will tell you, auspicious one, for you are devoted and dear to me.
Formerly, in the Kṛta age, O goddess, all people of purified mind / worship Viṣṇu alone, knowing him to be the Lord of the lords of all.
They attain the supreme prosperity, of this world and the next, O dear one, / which all the celestials and sages, accompanied by suffering, did not attain.
Those who have made resolve in the name attain that destination. / Even after hearing from my mouth, the gods are turned away from Viṣṇu.
With minds bewildered by different Vedas, Purāṇas, and established doctrines, / they do not arrive at a certainty: “What is reality? What is the supreme state?”
By gifts such as weighing against gold, by sacrifices such as the horse sacrifice, / by bathing in holy places such as Vārāṇasī and Prayāga, O dear one,
by ancestral rites such as the Gaya śrāddha, by recitations such as the study of the Vedas, / by fierce austerities, observances, restraints, and compassion for living beings,
by attending upon gurus, by practicing dharmas associated with classes and stages of life, / by knowledge and meditation, well practiced through ten million births,
[men] do not reach that supreme good, [whereas] resorting with all their being / to Viṣṇu, the Lord of the lords of all, the ancient Supreme Person,
mortals who have no other refuge, even if devoted to sensual pleasures, O scorcher of foes, / though devoid of knowledge and detachment, and lacking celibacy and the like,

Deprived of all religious duties, reciting only the name of Viṣṇu,
[such people] attain with ease that state which not even all the righteous reach.

Viṣṇu is to be remembered constantly; he is never to be forgotten.
All injunctions and prohibitions are merely servants to this alone.

Indeed, gods such as Brahmā and the sinless sages
have fearlessly attained their desired abode through the name of Viṣṇu alone.

And not having received worship for myself, Hari was thoroughly propitiated
by me, proud-minded, desiring what is even greater than this.

Then Keśava, the lord of the universe, pleased and affectionate toward his devotees,
personally worshipped them through portions of his own self:

the merciful one [worshipped] the gods, the ancestors, and the twice-born with oblations, ancestral offerings, and the like.
From that time forward, they are worthy of worship in the three worlds containing both the moving and the unmoving,

all the gods headed by Brahmā, by the grace of the wielder of the bow Śārṅga.
And he said to me: 'You shall become superior and worthy of worship even beyond me.

Having thus propitiated you, O Śambhu, I will always receive a boon.
Having appeared in human form and other manifestations at the beginning of the Dvāpara and other ages,

turn people away from me by means of scripture devised by yourself,
and conceal me, so that this continuous creation may proceed.

I quickly emit this delusion that will confound mankind,
and you, O mighty-armed Rudra, compose delusion-producing treatises.

Display things that are untrue and unfounded, O long-armed one;
make yourself manifest, and keep me concealed.'

Then, having bowed down to that Supreme Lord, I said:
'The sin of a thousand slayings of Brahmins might somehow be extinguished,

but never the lack of knowledge of you, even in hundreds of millions of kalpas.
Therefore, rivalry was undertaken by me; how may I become purified, O Hari?

Tell that expiation to me, O Govinda, if you wish.'
Then the pleased Lord revealed his true nature,

by which I became greater than that, O daughter of the mountain.
Him alone do I constantly worship with penance, praise, and contemplate.

Viṣṇu alone is the supreme one; knowledge of him is the means to liberation.
This indeed is the definitive conclusion of the scriptures; everything else is for the sake of delusion.

And [the notion of] liberation without gift-giving, my equality with Viṣṇu,
knowledge arising merely from sacred pilgrimage places and the like, my superiority over Viṣṇu,

and the non-difference of beings such as us, as well as liberated souls, from Hari—
all such things are stated for delusion, O virtuous woman, and not otherwise.
Because of him, I possess peerless majesty and am worshipped by the universe, O Pārvatī.

Pārvatī said:
Tell me that, O Lord of the gods, O Śaṅkara, so that I too,
O Lord, may become the incomparable sovereign of all, resembling you.

Mahādeva said:
Well asked, well asked by you, O beloved, concerning the divine Viṣṇu!
I shall proclaim the thousand names, supreme and bestowing liberation upon the three worlds.

Of this hymn of a thousand names of the venerable Viṣṇu, the venerable Mahādeva is the seer, the metre is anuṣṭubh,

the seed-syllable is hrīṃ, the power is śrīṃ, the pin is klīṃ; the application is in recitation for the sake of the four aims of life: dharma, sensual pleasure, wealth, and liberation.

To whom fortune is obedient, motionless, the giver of fortune, Viṣṇu, whose abode is the milk ocean, / whose chest is illuminated by the Kaustubha gem, Mādhava, who removes the distress of the world,
whose chest bears the Śrīvatsa mark, the vessel of limitless auspicious qualities, / dressed in yellow robes, the Lord of the world, protector of the world, father of the world,
Kin to the world, creator of the world, sustainer of the world, treasure of the world, / sole manifester of energy in the world, free from egotism, identical with the world,
composed of all wonders, who has accomplished all goals, delighting everyone, / whose efforts are always unfailing, the supreme consciousness of Brahmā, Rudra, and others,
the grandfather of Śambhu, the father of Brahmā, the supreme ruler of Śakra and the rest, / dear to all gods, the embodiment of all gods, having no superior,
the sole refuge of all gods, the single deity of all gods, / the enjoyer of sacrifices, the giver of the fruit of sacrifices, the Lord of sacrifice, the promoter of sacrifice,

the protector of sacrifice, the sacrificial person, wearing a garland of forest flowers, dear to the twice-born, / who uniquely bestows honour upon the twice-born, family deity of the Brahmins, destroyer of the Asuras,
the destroyer of all evil ones, the sole protector of all good people, / who holds the seven worlds in his belly alone, the sole ornament of the seven worlds,

the author of creation, preservation, and dissolution, wielding the discus, bearing the Śārṅga bow, holding the mace, / holding the conch, bearing the Nandaka sword, lotus-handed, mounted upon Garuḍa,
whose form is indescribable, worthy of all worship, the purifier of the three worlds, / whose renown is endless, of limitless prowess, universally auspicious,
radiant as ten million suns, unapproachable as ten million Yamas, / creator of the world like ten million Mayas, mighty as ten million winds,
gladdening the world like ten million moons, the great lord like ten million Śambhus, / beautiful as ten million Kamas, crushing enemies like ten million Durgas,
unfathomable as ten million oceans, bearing names like ten million sacred places, / endowed with fortune like ten million Kuberas, possessing sport like ten million Śakras,
unshakeable as ten million Himalayas, whose form comprises ten million universes, / destroyer of sins like ten million horse sacrifices, equal in worship to ten million sacrifices,
the cause of well-being like ten million nectars, granting desires like ten million wish-fulfilling cows, / whose form embodies ten million sacred sciences, Śipiviṣṭa, Śuciśravas,
supporter of the universe, whose feet are sacred bathing-places, hearing and chanting of whom brings merit, / the primal god, conqueror of the world, Mukunda, slayer of Kālanemi,
abiding in Vaikuṇṭha, of limitless majesty, the festival of the great lords of yoga, / eternally contented, of shining essence, free from doubt, the destroyer of Naraka,
the sole refuge of the poor and helpless, the sole dispeller of the universe's distress, / ever endowed with mercy toward the world, compassionate, the shelter of the virtuous,
the Lord of yoga, ever elevated, devoid of increase and decay, / Adhokṣaja, seed of the universe, lord over a hundred Prajāpatis,
whose feet are worshipped by Śakra and Brahmā, dwelling in the realm above Śambhu and Brahmā, / whose eyes are the sun and the moon, enjoyer of the universe, reaching beyond everything,
the bridge of the world, the bridge of dharma, the bearer, carrying the burden of the universe, / free from possessiveness, Lord of all the worlds, unattached, enjoying wondrous pleasures,
to whom illusion is subject, to whom the universe is subject, Viṣvaksena, the best among the gods, / the lord of all auspiciousness, adorned with divine and priceless ornaments,
marked by all auspicious marks, destroyer of the pride of all Daitya lords, / the all-in-all of all the gods, the leader of all deities,
the armor of all gods, the crest-jewel of all gods, / the fortress of all deities, an adamantine cage for those who take refuge,
whose name removes all fears, the Blessed Lord, Viṣṭaraśravas, / all-pervading, whose consequences bring universal welfare, who slays enemies and bestows heaven and liberation,
the Lord of the life of all deities, who appoints the Brahmins and others [to their duties], / Brahmā and Śambhu, whose lifespan is two parārdhas, the eldest before Brahmā, an infant, sovereign,

universal sovereign, dependent upon his devotees, worthy of praise, fulfilling the purpose of hymns of praise, / accomplishing the goals of others, knowing what must be done, ever free from actions for selfish ends,
ever blissful, ever auspicious, ever peaceful, ever benevolent, / ever beloved, ever satisfied, ever nourished, ever worshipped,
ever pure, foremost among purifiers, hidden in the Vedas, Vṛṣākapi, / having a thousand names, appearing in three ages, possessing four forms, four-armed,
lord of past, future, and present, the firstborn of the supreme spirit, / Nārāyaṇa, Muñjakeśa, emerged from all yoga,
the essence of the Vedas, essence of sacrifice, essence of the Sāman, treasury of asceticism, / the Sādhya, the highest, the ancient sage, firm resolve, tranquility, the ultimate resort,
destroyer of Śiva’s trident, the sole bestower of boons on Śrīkaṇṭha, / Nara, Kṛṣṇa, Hari, the son of Dharma, the life of Dharma,
the primeval creator, wholly true, destroyer of the pride of all jewel-like women, / conqueror of Kama through the three times, creator of Urvaśī, lord among sages,
the primeval poet, Hayagrīva, master of all lords of speech, / composed of all gods, Brahmā, the guru, lord of the goddess of speech,
source of endless learning, destroyer of fundamental ignorance, / omniscient, dispeller of the world’s dullness, Madhusūdana,
lord over tens of millions of diverse mantras, who alone has mastered Śabdabrahman, / the primal scholar, author of the Vedas, the soul of the Vedas, ocean of the sacred scriptures,
who seized back the Vedas for Brahmā's sake, birthplace of all specialized knowledge, / king of sciences, embodiment of wisdom, ocean of knowledge, of unbroken intellect,
the divine Fish, huge-horned, guiding the ship containing the seeds of the world, / pervading the entire ocean in sport, promulgator of the four Vedas,
the primal Tortoise, foundation of all, rendering the weight of the universe like a blade of grass, / who made the host of gods immortal, the cause of the emergence of nectar,
supported by himself, supporter of the earth, his limbs consisting of sacrifice, upholder of the earth, / slayer of Hiraṇyākṣa, lord of the earth, author of ancestor rites and the rest,
slayer of fear for all the ancestors, the life of all the ancestors, / sole enjoyer of oblations to gods and ancestors, sole giver of the fruits of oblations to gods and ancestors,
in the pores of whose skin the oceans vanished, who agitated the boundless seas, / the Great Boar, destroyer of those who ruin sacrifices, haven of those who perform sacrifices,
the glorious Narasiṃha, divine lion, removing all undesired things and sorrows, / the solitary hero, of wondrous strength, sole destroyer of [hostile] yantras and mantras,
whose brilliance is unbearable to Brahmā and the rest, exceedingly dreadful at the end of an aeon, / whose claws surpass ten million thunderbolts, assuming a form hard for the world to look upon,
crusher of the circle of mothers, lord of the host of Great Mothers, / endowed with inconceivable and unfailing power, devourer of all Asuras,
the slayer of Hiraṇyakaśipu, Death, lord of Saṃkarṣaṇī, / irresistible to the mount of Death, destroyer of all fears,
destroyer of all obstacles, giver of all accomplishments, fulfiller of all desires, / annihilator of all sins, whose name is superior to accomplished mantras,
Lord of the Bhairavas, dispeller of Śiva’s affliction, unapproachable as ten million Deaths, / whose name causes the fetuses of Daityas to miscarry, whose roar splits the universe,
protector of everything upon merely being remembered, of wondrous form, the great Hari, / with an orb of skulls of celibacy, whose higher limbs are adorned by the guardians of the directions,
wearing a garland made of the heads of the twelve Ādityas, having Rudra’s head as a single anklet, / rescuer of Girijā when seized by the Yoginīs, terrifying Bhairava,
Lord of the circle of heroes, exceedingly fierce, enemy of Apasmāra, death to Śambara, / Lord of wrath, consumer of the wicked retinues of Rudracaṇḍī and others,
unshakable by all, death to Death, who averts premature death, / slayer of all incurable diseases, making all malevolent planets benevolent,
destroyer of the pride of ten million Gaṇeśas, destroyer of unbearable, endless clans, / difficult to behold by gods and Dānavas, terrifying to the terrors of the world,

savior from all misfortune, devourer of the devourers of the world, / the fierce cat to Śambara, devourer of the mouse of Time, / whose staff-like arms hold endless weapons, Narasiṃha, who conquered Vīrabhadra.
The secret lord of the circle of yoginīs, the consumer of the meat of Indra's sacrificial beast, / Rudra, Nārāyaṇa, the mount of Śaṅkara in the form of a ram,
The savior of Śiva who took the form of a ram, the consumer of thousands of wicked powers, / The beloved of Tulasī, the hero, the left-hand path practitioner, the granter of all desires,
Mahāśiva, mounted on Śivā, the sole bearer of Bhairava's skull, / The lord of the wheel of pins, the giver of a divine and enchanting form to Indra,
The giver of good fortune to Gaurī, the treasure of māyā, the remover of fear caused by māyā, / Composed of the splendor of Brahman, composed of the glory of Brahman, and composed of the three Vedas,
Subrahmaṇya, the destroyer of Bali, Vāmana, the remover of Aditi's sorrow, / Upendra, the king, Viṣṇu, the ornament of Kaśyapa's lineage,
The giver of his own kingdom to Bali, the giver of food to all gods and brāhmaṇas, Acyuta, / Of mighty strides, whose feet are sacred waters, who stands on three steps, Trivikrama,
Whose foot reached the sky, who sanctified the three worlds with the water from his feet, / Whose feet are worshiped by Brahmā, Īśa, and others, whose feet were washed by the flowing Dharma,
Of inconceivable and wondrous expanse, the world-tree, possessed of great strength, / The cutter of Rāhu's head and other limbs, the severer of the head of Bhṛgu's wife,
Afraid of sin, ever meritorious, the perpetual shatterer of the hopes of the Daityas, / The fulfiller of all the gods' hopes, the maker of incarnations solely for the world's welfare,
Whose self is ever concealed by his own māyā, ever a wish-fulfilling jewel for his devotees, / The giver of boons, the bestower of kingship upon kings such as Kārttavīrya, the sinless one,
Whose conduct is praised by the world and boundless, Dattātreya, the lord of sages, / Ever embraced by the supreme power, the bliss of yoga, ever ecstatically intoxicated,
The taker of the splendor of all enemies of Indra, the drinker of the lotus of supreme nectar, / The jewel of Anusūyā's womb, the bestower of the happiness of enjoyment and liberation,
The sun of Jamadagni's lineage, the maker of wondrous power in Reṇukā, / Untainted by matricide and other acts, the conqueror of Skanda, the giver of a kingdom to brāhmaṇas,
The ender of all kṣatriyas, the destroyer of the pride of heroes, the conqueror of Kārttavīrya, / The donor of the earth with its seven continents, the bestower of renown upon the worshiper of Śiva,
Terrific, Paraśurāma, the sole world-protector following Śiva's teachings, / The treasure-house of all Śiva's knowledge, the teacher of Bhīṣma, having fire as deity,
The guru of Droṇācārya, whose bow conquered the universe, the conqueror of Kṛtānta, / The embodiment of peerless asceticism, whose only sacrificial fee was celibacy,
Manu, the best, the extended sacrificial session of the virtuous, the most venerable, Ṛṣabha, the cosmic sovereign, / The primordial king, the father of the earth, the sole milker of all jewels,
Pṛthu, uniquely capable from his very birth, chosen by Speech, Śrī, and Renown of their own accord, / The giver of livelihood to the world, the foremost of emperors, the wielder of twin weapons,
Attainable by sages such as Sanaka, the nourisher of devotion to the Blessed Lord, / The author, teacher, and promoter of the duties of castes and stages of life,
The banner of the solar dynasty, Rāma, Rāghava, the ocean of good qualities, / Kākutstha, the king of heroes, the king, the bearer of the burden of royal duty,

The eternal refuge of the composed, the receiver of all auspiciousness, seeing only good, / The jewel among men, containing jewels in his womb, the overseer of dharma, the great treasure, / The refuge of all excellent beings, endowed with the potency of the whole collection of scriptural meanings,
Holding the world under sway, the son of Daśaratha, the king who is the refuge of all jewels, / The source of all dharmas, the seer of all dharmas, the destroyer of all sins,

He transcends Indra, has reached the other shore of knowledge and higher wisdom, and is an ocean of patience; / he is cherished by the most distinguished and righteous, untroubled by joy and grief; / he abandoned an empire at his father's command, fearless at the rise of adversity.
He bestowed sovereignty upon the region of Guha, bore matted hair rivaling Śiva's; / he obtained the jewel-like mountain of Citrakūṭa, wandering in the forest as the Lord of the world.

He whose every missile was unfailing according to his will, who destroyed the eye of Indra's son, / who directed the reed blade bowed to by Brahmā and Indra, the slayer of Mārīca, the slayer of Virādha;
The purifier of the entire Daṇḍaka forest struck down by a brāhmaṇa's curse; / who bore a single arrow that slew fourteen thousand ferocious rākṣasas;
The enemy of Khara, the slayer of Triśiras, the slayer of Dūṣaṇa, the tormentor of enemies; / who gave the path of fire to Jaṭāyu, the all-in-all of Agastya, the king of mantras;
Who in sport kicked away the vast heap of Dundubhi's bones with the tip of his bow; / who with the piercing of the seven sāla trees cast down and destroyed the dānavas of the nether world;
Who gave the kingdom to Sugrīva, granting fearlessness to the lowly by his mere thought; / who assumed the body of every monkey, chief among them Hanumat and Rudra;
Who agitated the ocean with a single arrow shot along with the Nāgas and Daityas; / who dried and burned the ocean with a single arrow directed against millions of mlecchas;
The storehouse of fame who built a bridge across the ocean, an unprecedented marvel; / who accomplishes the impossible, skilled in uprooting the entirety of Laṅkā;

The destroyer of the lineage of Paulastya, that dart in the world arrogant with boons; / the slayer of Rāvaṇa's son [Indrajit], the killer of Prahasta, the splitter of Kumbhakarṇa, the slayer of the fierce;
The severer of Rāvaṇa's heads, the giver of fear-free, sole sovereignty to Indra; / the destroyer of heaven and non-heaven, the remover of the humiliation of the king of gods;

He who stripped the demons of their godliness, the destroyer of righteousness and unrighteousness, praised by many; / the enemy of the Ten-headed who granted the kingdom to Vibhīṣaṇa merely upon his bow;
The sole reviver of his entire army that had died, by a shower of nectar; / the single creator of the name of gods and brāhmaṇas, worshipped by all the immortals;
Whose beloved, faithful wife was returned by the hosts of Brahmā, Sūrya, Indra, Rudra, and others; / the king of all in Ayodhyā, captivating to all beings;

Whose mercy and punishment were equal for masters and servants, who loved only the virtuous, whether low or high; / who viewed justice beginning with his own side, who accomplished great things for the destitute;

Who acted inappropriately under the pretext of a hunter, the savior, who treats all equally; / whose soul was freed by Pārvatī's superiority, abandoned by his beloved, the conqueror of the enemy of Smara [Śiva];
Directly the father of Indra and others disguised as Kuśa and Lava, undefeated; / the lord of Kośala, mighty-armed, who abandoned his brother for the sake of truth;
By the fitting of whose arrow the emergence of the terrestrial orb was shaken; / who gave masters to the deities through his presence, which is desired by Brahmā and others;

Who brought the entire company of living beings, beginning with the caṇḍālas, to the world of Brahmā; / who led donkeys, horses, and others along with himself, the sole protector of Ayodhyā for long ages;
He who was his second self, Saumitri Lakṣmaṇa, the slayer of Indrajit; / who found contentment in the kingdom of Rāma's sandals, attained through devotion to Viṣṇu;
Bharata, the slayer of crores of unendurable gandharvas; the ender of Lavaṇa, / Śatrughna; the king of physicians, who holds the Āyurveda in his womb, the lord of medicinal herbs;
Dhanvantari, who eternally produces nectar; the Sacrifice, the supporter of the world; / the slayer of the enemy of the sun, the life of the gods, the lord of the south, beloved of the twice-born;

Whose severed head was the sun of that region, who established the gods in his remaining limbs; / whose form was uninjured by the cutting off of his head with all Kadrū's weapons for the sake of the universe;
The sacred fire bearing names such as Vājapeya, devoted to the duty of the Vedas; / the lord of Śvetadvīpa, the expounder of Sāṃkhya, the king of all spiritual perfections;
The dispeller of the darkness of delusion through the yoga of knowledge revealed to the universe; / the son of Devahūti, the accomplished Siddha Kapila, the son of Kardama;
The master of yoga who turned the sons of Sagara to ash for breaking his meditation; / Dharma, the chief bull, the lord of Surabhi, realized by the pure-minded;
Śambhu, the bearer of the universe-chariot for the sole stability in burning the triple city; / conquered by his devotee Śambhu, the entire drinker of the nectar-well of the Daityas;
The king of all Nāgas, who alone remains at the great dissolution of the universe; / Lord Śeṣa, thousand-eyed, with a thousand mouths, heads, and arms;
Upon the particles of whose hood-gems the oceans, waters, and earth are placed; / the father of Kālāgnirudra, armed with a pestle, carrying a plow as weapon;
Dressed in blue garments, the lord of Vāruṇī, the remover of sins of mind, speech, and body; / insatiable, who brought down the single ten-headed one by a mere glance;
The binder of Bali, terrible, the son of Rohiṇī, the slayer of Pralamba; / the slayer of Muṣṭika, the slayer of Dvivida, the dragger of the Kālindī, Bala [Balarāma];
The lover of Revatī, the elder brother of Acyuta out of fatigue from earlier devotion; / the son of Kaśyapa and Aditi known under the names of Devakī and Vasudeva;
The descendant of Vṛṣṇi, the best of the Sātvatas, Śauri, the upholder of the Yadu race; / the supreme Brahman in human form, the giver of boons to Savyasācin [Arjuna];
Whose infancy was a wonder to the world, charming and desired even by Brahmā and others; / the slayer of Pūtanā, the shatterer of the cart, the breaker of the twin arjuna trees;
The enemy of the demon Vāta, the slayer of Keśin, the enemy of Dhenuka, the lord of cattle; / Dāmodara, the god of cowherds, the giver of joy to Yaśodā and Nanda;
The crusher of Kālīya, dear to all the cowherds and gopīs; / who held Govardhana in play, Govinda, the festival of Gokula;
The crusher of Ariṣṭa, the giver of liberation to the gopīs intoxicated with desire; / the immediate slayer of Kuvalayāpīḍa, the crusher of Cāṇūra;
The enemy of Kaṃsa, whose other deeds included establishing Ugrasena and others in the kingdom; / who adorned the earthly world with the Sudharmā council hall, the ender of the army of Jarāsandha;
Who let the defeated Jarāsandha go, the giver of glory to Bhīmasena; / the giver back of Sāndīpani's dead child, the conqueror of Kāla, Antaka, and others;
The savior of all denizens of hell, the conqueror of tens of millions of all kings; / the lover of Rukmiṇī, the punisher of Rukmin, the destroyer of Naraka;
The beloved of all beautiful women, the enemy of Mura, whose banner is Garuḍa; / who alone conquered Rudra, Sūrya, the Maruts, and all the other lords;
The destroyer of the pride of Indra, who adorned the earth with the wish-granting tree; / who together with cutting off the arms of Bāṇa conquered millions of the hosts of Nandī and others;
Who defeated Mahādeva in sport, who alone was worshipped by Mahādeva; / who granted unbroken victory to Arjuna for Indra's sake, the sole supporter of the Pāṇḍavas;
The severer of the head of the king of Kāśī, the sole crusher of Rudra's power; / whose glance was the grace of Viśveśvara, the tormentor of the son of the king of Kāśī;
The destroyer of Śambhu's pledge, the leader who burned Kāśī; / the slayer of millions who went with the lord of Kāśī, who worshipped brāhmaṇas to instruct the world;
Submissive to the vows of young women, who of old granted boons to Śiva; / the sole sustainer of Śaṅkara's installation, who worshipped Śaṅkara as an aspect of himself;

The lord of the vow of the maiden for Śiva, the slayer of Śiva's enemies in the form of Kṛṣṇa; / having the body of Mahālakṣmī, the protector of Gaurī, the slayer of the demon Vṛtra with half-broken pieces;
Who drove away the Yavana into his own abode to fulfill Mucukunda's wish; / the lord of the Yamunā, who brought back the departed sons of the brāhmaṇa;
Who brought Indra's opulence down to earth for the sake of his poor devotee Śrīdāman; / who gave sole liberation to the wicked Śiśupāla, the lord of Dvārakā;
Who established crores of treasures in Dvārakā, accessible down to the caṇḍālas; / the giver of free liberation to his foremost devotees headed by Akrūra and Uddhava;
Who turned the ocean into a pool of nectar for water sports with children and women; / the sole reviver of Parīkṣit within the womb, who was burned by the missile of Brahmā;
The bringer back of the departed sons of the brāhmaṇa, the remover of Arjuna's pride; / who swallowed up all the Kauravas headed by Bhīṣma under the guise of an enigmatic form;
Who shattered every divine weapon truly, the dispeller of Pārtha's delusion; / who removed the fear of the earth by destroying the Yādavas through the pretext of a curse of the womb;
The giver of a higher state to his enemy, the hunter Jarā; the granter of all desires upon mere recollection; / Kāmadeva, the husband of Rati, Manmatha, the destroyer of Śambara;
The bodiless Anaṅga, who conquered the lord of Gaurī; the lover of Rati, ever desired; / who has flowers for arrows, the conqueror of the universe, Smara, beloved of Kāmeśvarī.
The husband of Uṣā, having the universe as his banner, proud in all things, the supreme person, / Having four selves, having four manifestations, the ordainer of the four ages,
The sole cosmic self of the four Vedas, possessing millions of supreme portions, / The self of the life-stages, the ancient sage, Vyāsa, the creator of thousands of Vedic branches,
The author of the Mahābhārata, the king of poets, Bādarāyaṇa, / Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana, the sole teacher of all aims of human life,
The author of the Vedānta, the sole revealer of Brahman, the founder of the Puru lineage, / The Buddha, who conquered all the gods of gods through meditation, dear to the world,
Unarmed, conquering the world, Śrīdhara, the deluder of the wicked, / Casting the Daityas outside the Veda, the concealer of the Vedic texts and the meaning of the Veda,
The son of Śuddhodana, of sharp vision, the giver of happiness, the lord of the assembly, / Merciful to all as appropriate, the void of everything, the giver of all desires,
The principle distinct from the four alternatives, the lord of the perfection of wisdom, / The lord of the path of heretics and the Veda, the concealer of heretical revelations,
Kalki, the son of Viṣṇuyaśas, the destroyer of the Kali age, / The slayer of all wicked barbarians, the maker of all twice-born men well-disciplined,
The initiator of the Kṛta age, the remover of the prolonged hunger of gods and twice-born, / Revanta among cavalrymen and the like, the destroyer of the earth's distress,
Instantly making the fortune of the earth bow [before him], knowing the entirety of lost dharma, / Filling all twice-born with gold solely through the infinite conjunction of gold,
The sole ruler of the untamable world, praiseworthy to the universe, whose banner is victory, / The master of the self-principle, the best of agents, Vidhi, the lord of Umā,
Best of protectors, foremost of lords of creatures, Marīci, leader among progenitors, / Kaśyapa, Indra king of the gods, Prahlāda king of the daityas, the Moon,
The lord of asterisms, the Sun, the best of splendors, Śukra the lord of poets, / Bhṛgu the king of great sages, Viṣṇu, the lord of Ādityas, Bali the sovereign,
Wind, Fire, the best purifier, Śaṅkara the king of Rudras, the Teacher, / The most learned, Citraratha the foremost of Gandharvas, the best imperishable [syllable],
The foremost of colors and letters, Gaurī among women, Śrī among powers, and Nārada / The king of divine sages, Arjuna the foremost of the Pāṇḍavas, philosophical discussion the king of debates,
The wind, the wind-god, Varuṇa the lord of aquatic creatures, / The Gaṅgā the best of holy fords, gambling the foremost of deceits, food the supreme medicine,
Food, Sudarśana the foremost of missiles, the thunderbolt the best of weapons, / Uccaiḥśravas the king of horses, Airāvata the lord of elephants,
Arundhatī the mistress of faithful wives, the aśvattha the king of all trees, / The science of the self the foremost of sciences, the praṇava the best of meters,
Meru the lord of mountains, Mārgaśīrṣa the foremost of months, the best of times, / The soul of day and other divisions, Kapila the ancient adept, the Sāmaveda the king [of Vedas],
Garuḍa the king of birds, Spring the foremost of seasons, the wish-yielding tree / The best of givers, the wish-fulfilling cow, the foremost remover of distress, the truest friend,
The wish-granting jewel, the best guru, mother, most beneficent father, / The lion the king of beasts, Vāsuki the king of serpents, the king the foremost of men,
The brāhmaṇa the lord of castes, the mind, the foremost compassion—obeisance, obeisance! / Thus this thousand names of Vāsudeva Viṣṇu
Allays all offenses and supremely increases devotion; / It is the imperishable, sole means to attain all heavens, beginning with the world of Brahmā.
It is the sole ladder to Viṣṇu's realm, the destroyer of all sorrow, / The bestower of all happiness, granting supreme liberation immediately.
It purifies completely the mind's defilements such as desire and anger; / It gives peace and purifies human beings, even great sinners.
It quickly yields the fruit of all desires to all living beings, / Pacifies all obstacles, and destroys all misfortunes.
It allays terrible sorrow, destroys acute poverty, / Removes the three debts, is secret, and brings wealth, grain, and renown.
It gives all sovereignty, grants all perfections, bestows all dharma, / And yields the fruit of tens of millions of holy fords, sacrifices, austerities, gifts, and vows.
It calms the dullness of the world, promotes all knowledge, / Gives kingdoms to those fallen from power, and cures all diseases of the sick.
It gives sons to barren women, and grants life to those whose lifespan is depleted; / It destroys ghosts, seizing spirits, and poison, and eliminates the affliction of evil planets.
It is auspicious, meritorious, and prolongs life through hearing, reciting, or muttering; / By [reciting] it once, all the Vedas with their auxiliary limbs and millions of mantras [are recited].
The Purāṇas, treatises, and Smṛtis will be heard and recited, / and if one mutters a single syllable, verse, or line, O beloved,
every desire is constantly accomplished without delay—how much more all of them? / There is nothing equal to this, giving immediate certainty in all deeds.
This must be kept secret by you, auspicious one, and recited only for the accomplishment of your own goal; / it must not be given to a non-Vaiṣṇava whose mind is ruined by doubt,
who lacks devotion and faith, and who regards Viṣṇu as ordinary. / It may be given to a son, a pupil, or a friend out of desire for their welfare.
Except through my grace, those of small intelligence will not grasp this. / In the Kali age, Nārada will bring to Kalpagrāma this fruit that yields immediate results,
by which the sorrow of unfortunate people is destroyed. / In Āryāvarta it will be present among a few Vaiṣṇavas.
There is no abode higher than Viṣṇu; there is no asceticism higher than Viṣṇu; / there is no dharma higher than Viṣṇu; and there is no mantra that is not related to Viṣṇu.
There is no truth higher than Viṣṇu; there is no sacrifice higher than Viṣṇu; / there is no meditation higher than Viṣṇu; there is no path higher than Viṣṇu.
What need has he of many mantras, or of extensive treatises, / or of thousands of Vājapeya sacrifices, who has devotion to Janārdana?

Viṣṇu consists of all holy sites; the Lord consists of all treatises; / Viṣṇu consists of all sacrifices—truly, truly do I say! / The essential substance up to Brahmā, all this has been declared by me.
Pārvatī said: / I am blessed, I am favored, I have achieved my aim, O lord of the world, / since I have heard this hymn, your very rare secret.
Alas, what a great distress that even though Hari, the lord of the gods, the destroyer of all sorrow, / is present, fools suffer in the cycle of transmigration!
Directing himself constantly toward which Lord, even Maheśa / is seen by people sky-clad, matted-haired, his body smeared with ashes, an ascetic?
What god is higher than him, the beloved of Lakṣmī, the enemy of Madhu, / whose reality is constantly meditated upon by you yourself, the lord of yoga?
What higher station is there beyond Śrī Puruṣottama? / Not knowing him, whom do fools, proud of their knowledge, worship?
I was deceived by you for a long time, O lord, in that this Sovereign / was not revealed to me, from whom proceed divine powers beginning with you.
Ah, Viṣṇu, the Lord of all, the highest of all gods, / the teacher of those beginning with you, is seen by fools as merely ordinary!
Such is the greatness of the great: they favor those who worship them, / and, endowed with forbearance, they disregard even the wicked who hate them.
In my childhood, too, the subjects of my father were seen by me to be hungry; / unable to sustain them out of distress, they were supported after worshipping Lakṣmī.
Because of her proximity, the subjects and those beginning with you, / along with Śakra and the others, sports together with friends, allies, and kin.
Without her, where is divinity? Where is sovereignty? Where are possessions? / All living beings would exist dwelling only in torments.
Without her, dharma, wealth, pleasure, and even liberation are far away; / for those who are hungry and destitute, whence could come yoga and meditation?
And he is the sole essence of the world, the sole leader of all the worlds, / under whose control is Kamalā, having abandoned even whom Śaṅkara [wanders]—
of that great soul who is complete in freedom from arrogance, purity, beauty, wealth of uprightness, / and pre-eminent valor in all things.
Who can attain equality with him, Viṣṇu, the god of gods, / without whose portion of a portion of descent everything dissolves?
The deluded, nevertheless, say that this world exists for flaw; / he has neither birth nor death, nor anything unobtainable for his own purpose.
Because my mind is attached to desire and the like, however, O sovereign Lord, / or because of absorption in you, or out of negligence, if I am unable to recite
this Thousand Names of Viṣṇu every day, O Bull-bannered One, / tell me, O Lord, the single name by which the same fruit is attained.
Mahādeva said: / 'Rāma, Rāma, Rāma'—delighting in Rāma, the charming one! / The name of Rāma, O fair-faced one, is equal to the thousand names.

6.72.m: Thus ends the seventy-first chapter, named the Complete Thousand Names of Viṣṇu, in the dialogue between the Lord of Umā and Nārada, in the Uttarakhaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Purāṇa, a compendium of fifty-five thousand [verses].
one attains liberation lasting as long as the dissolution of the elements. / The Thousand Names of Viṣṇu along with the ritual placement, O goddess,

6.73.m: recited by the best of men, leads them to the imperishable abode. / Whoever recites it once, twice, or thrice a day,

6.74.m:
Listen, O goddess, I will declare the glorification of Keśava; / the best of men who hear it are meritorious and embody merit.

Mahādeva said: / Listen, O goddess, I shall proclaim the supreme glorification of dharma, / hearing which, one is never again born on earth.
From dharma one obtains purpose, desire, and liberation—these three. / Therefore, the learned man should strive for dharma; he is regarded as wise.
Through asceticism, through gift-giving, through vow and observance, / through asceticism that is sattvic, heaven is likewise attained.
Arrived here, free from anger and greed, he obtains a kingdom; / in another birth there will be liberation, and he attains the Vaiṣṇava state.
Through asceticism of passion, he is born here endowed with passion; / having practiced austerity with an attitude of darkness, he is cruel in action and harsh.
That austerity is said to belong to demons, granting enjoyment to those of dark nature. / Whatever austerity is performed that is sattvic, that alone is true austerity.

In the forest, of the good who subsist on wind in absolute solitude, austerity is bound by passion and darkness; / and of ascetics desiring wealth and the like, even in the forest, faults arise for the passionate.

Even at home, restraint of the five senses is austerity for one who engages in blameless action; / for one whose passion has ceased, the house is an ascetic grove; therefore the householder order is declared as one's own duty.

Very hard to traverse, for those who conquer the senses by goodness, the most supreme and auspicious stage of life is secured; / for the householder's dharma is the best of the wise, declared by Brahmā and the rest, O mountain's daughter.

Having practiced austerity in the forest, the ascetic, afflicted with hunger, always comes to the house of the giver of food; / and he gives food to him with devotion, [and so] shares in a portion of his austerity.

Whatever person properly protects the householder order, the eldest of orders here, / enjoying human pleasures in this very world, he goes to heaven—there is no doubt here. / For how can sin approach men who always maintain a household, O goddess?
The householder order is the most meritorious; the home is always like a sacred ford. / In this meritorious householder order, gifts should especially be given.
Where there is worship of the gods and the feeding of guests, / and shelter for travelers, it is therefore considered most blessed.
Depending upon that house, those men who worship twice-borns / never suffer the loss of lifespan, wealth, and sons.
Listen, O beautiful lady, I shall explain the purifier of great sins: / the gift that brings all prosperity and bestows fruits here and hereafter.
When an auspicious time has arrived, having worshipped one's own deity / and performed the daily and occasional rites, one should give a gift according to one's capacity.
Even having seized another's wealth, if one gives it only to twice-borns and the gods, / after seeing hell he goes to the supreme state.
Just as Śatānīka was delivered from giving along with his son, / having given other [gifts] to twice-borns, he goes to heaven according to righteousness.
Of those by whom gifts were given in holy places, their dharma is spoken of. / Listen, O goddess, I shall explain the gift of wealth in brief.
A gift purifying the body has never been, nor will it ever be [equal to this]; / by which a man becomes free from sin, there is no doubt here.
Having enjoyed pleasures, he then goes to eternal Viṣṇu. / Formerly, indeed, it was told by Brahmā to the high-souled Bhārgava,
to Rāma who was afflicted with sin: the balance and the bull; / and the king devoted to sinful action, whose deeds cause worldly bondage,
those devoted to eating uneatable food, the slayer of an embryo, the violator of the guru's bed, / and these who speak untruth—they are born in non-human wombs.
Having performed sacrifices for those not entitled to sacrifice, having solicited the blameworthy, / always filled with anger, intent on tormenting the virtuous,
and those who destroy trust, censurers of dharma with their lives; / endowed with these sins, knowing oneself to have an exhausted lifespan,

6.74.s:

6.74.m:
Knowing this, O goddess, gifts especially ought to be given by them; / many performers of religious acts, Vaiṣṇavas, are renowned on earth.

The seventy-fifth chapter. / Mahādeva said: / I shall explain in accordance with the rule the glorification of the Gaṇḍakī, O goddess. / Just as the Gaṅgā is, so is she declared, O daughter of the mountain.

Where the Śālagrāma stone is born in many ways, / and its glorification was related by the best of sages,

where the egg-born, the plant-born, the sweat-born, and the womb-born, / merely by the sight of it, become forms of merit, O Pārvatī.

She arose in the north, the great river Gaṇḍakī; / remembered again and again, she surely destroys sin, O daughter of the mountain.

Where God Nārāyaṇa, the bestower of prosperity, constantly abides. / Those who dwell near her, bearing the conch and disc,

they, having reached death, have divine forms, four-armed. / The sages remain there, and the gods likewise in particular,

the Rudras, Nāgas, and Yakṣas—no doubt should be made here. / Near it is indeed this one place which bears the form of Viṣṇu.

In this place exists an image of multiple forms, granting great liberation; / there are indeed twenty-four types of beings there.

6.74.m:
One indeed has the form of a fish, and [another] the form of Kṛṣṇa granting great liberation; / and another which is declared by the wise in the place named after Viṣṇu,

likewise the meritorious one named Kalkin, [and] the brown one declared by me; / and others of various forms are also seen in many ways.

All the images remain in multiple forms, in many ways. / She is the great, meritorious Gaṅgā, granting dharma, desire, wealth, and liberation,

on which land Hṛṣīkeśa, accompanied by restraint, / dwells even today in that very place along with me—there is no doubt.

The killing of an embryo, the killing of a child, and especially the killing of a cow— / merely by her touch, one is freed from all sin.

Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, Śūdras, and other castes as well— / all of them are indeed liberated by the sight of the waters of the Gaṇḍakī.

She is equal to the Veṇī, meritorious especially for sinners; / where even a slayer of a Brahmin is freed, what then to speak of others?

"I always go there at all times, O Pārvatī. / Indeed, this king of sacred places was spoken of by Brahmā.

Bathing and giving gifts there have been prescribed by the sages. / In the month of Āṣāḍha, at that auspicious time, I go there, O lovely woman.

6.74.m:
According to the rules for one month, I perform my bath there; / there I constantly chant the clear, redeeming [mantra].

Therefore I have become a Vaiṣṇava, because I have gone to the realm of Viṣṇu. / That field fashioned of old by Viṣṇu is exceedingly great,

granting the highest state to Vaiṣṇavas, considered supremely purifying. / In this world, birth as a human being is always difficult to obtain, O goddess;

the Gaṇḍikā sacred place is difficult to attain, and the realm of Viṣṇu is difficult to attain. / Therefore, in the month of Āṣāḍha, the best of the twice-born should go there.

Having gone there, the best of the twice-born should especially bear / the conch, discus, and other marks; it is remembered as supremely purifying.

The conch sacred mark on the left side, and on the right side the mark of the discus; / it is declared to grant liberation to the twice-born, and should be worn with effort.

The bearing of the conch, discus, and other [marks] by Brahmins especially— / when it is worn, O great goddess, those humans are indeed Vaiṣṇavas.

There is no sacred place equal to the Gaṇḍikā, no vow equal to Dvādaśī, / and no god other than Keśava, again and again, O fair-faced woman!

Those best of men who hear the glorification of the Gaṇḍikā, / having enjoyed happiness in this world, indeed go to the world of Viṣṇu."

6.76.m: Mahādeva said: / "Listen, O lovely woman, I shall declare the hymn that brings prosperity, / hearing which even a sinner who has killed a Brahmin is freed, without a doubt.
The Creator spoke it to Nārada; that very thing I speak to you." / Then the self-born god of boundless splendor said to him,
holding his handsome arm and reminding him of his funeral rites: / "The blessed, glorious god Nārāyaṇa, Hari bearing the discus weapon,
holding the Śārṅga bow, Hṛṣīkeśa, the ancient supreme person, / unconquered, sword-bearing, victorious, and eternal Kṛṣṇa,
you are the one-horned boar, the essence of past, future, and present, / the imperishable, true Brahman, and Rāghava at the beginning and the end.
You are the supreme dharma of the worlds, Viṣvaksena, four-armed, / the army commander, the protector, Vaikuṇṭha, and lord of the universe.
You are the source and the imperishable, Upendra, the slayer of Madhu, / Pṛśnigarbha, bearer of brilliance, Padmanābha, ender of battles.
The great sages along with Indra declare you to be the refuge and shelter, / the best of the Ṛg and Sāma, the essence of the Veda, hundred-tongued, [honored by] great sages.
You are the sacrifice, you are the vaṣaṭ-call, you are the oṃkāra, O scorcher of foes, / Śatadhanvan, the Vasu of old, you are the Prajāpati of the Vasus,
the primal maker even of the three worlds, yourself the lord, / the eighth Rudra among the Rudras, and the fifth among the Sādhyas.
The two Aśvins are your ears, and the sun and moon are your eyes; / in the end, in the beginning, and in the middle, you are seen, O scorcher of foes!
Neither the origin nor the end of this [universe] do they know, [nor] who you are. / You are seen in all worlds, in cows, and in Brahmins,
in all directions, in the sky, on mountains, and in caves, / thousand-eyed, glorious, hundred-headed, thousand-footed.
You hold up the beings, and the earth together with its mountains; / within the earth, in the water, [you are] the great serpent of all living beings.
Supporting the three worlds, you abide, [holding] gods, Gandharvas, and Dānavas. / I am your heart, O Rāma; your tongue is goddess Sarasvatī.
The gods are the hairs on your limbs fashioned by your own creative power; / your closing of the eyes is considered the night, and opening of the eyes the day.
The bodily preparation is your body; nothing exists without you. / This whole universe is your body, and the firmness of the earth's surface [is you].
Fire is your anger, your grace is glorious Śeṣa, Lakṣmaṇa. / By you the three worlds were crossed with the three ancient strides.
By you Indra was made king, and the great Asura Bali was bound. / As Time, having dissolved the worlds and placed them within yourself alone,
you make a terrible single ocean, visible and invisible, not otherwise. / Having assumed the supreme, divine, excellent form of a lion,
you slew Hiraṇyakaśipu, who brought fear to all beings. / Having assumed a horse's face, you took refuge in the depths of the netherworld.
The supreme sacrificial offering, the secret [wisdom], was recovered again and again. / The light which is heard of as supreme, the one who is heard of as higher than the high,
and that which is higher than the highest, spoken of as the supreme self, / the supreme mantra, the supreme brilliance—you alone indeed are spoken of as that.

The offering to gods, the offering to ancestors, the purifier, and the attainment of heaven and liberation, / the maintenance, creation, and destruction are yours; they call you beyond material nature.
The sacrifice, the patron of the sacrifice, the hotṛ priest, and the adhvaryu priest, / and the enjoyer of the fruits of sacrifices—you indeed are sung by the Vedas.
Sītā is Lakṣmī, you are Viṣṇu, the divine Kṛṣṇa, Prajāpati; / for the sake of slaying Rāvaṇa, you entered a human body.
That task was accomplished by you, O best of upholders of dharma! / Rāvaṇa has been slain, O Rāma, and the deities have been made joyful.
Infallible is your divine vigor, your prowess is never futile, / infallible is the sight of you, O Rāma, and praise of you is never in vain.
Devoted men on earth will become unerring, / and those who are devoted to you, O god, the ancient supreme person.
This holy hymn of the ṛṣis, an ancient legendary history— / those men who recite it will suffer no defeat.
How indeed could the best of men, devoted to the supreme person, come to defeat here? / Indeed, in the world there is no deity superior in bestowing boons to those dear to the four-armed one.
This foremost of hymns among hymns, belonging to the great-souled Rāghava, / whoever recites it daily at the three twilight times, even if guilty of a great sin,
should be recited with effort by the best of the twice-born at the twilight time, / especially at the time of ancestral rites, with a mind full of devotion.
This is a supreme secret, not to be told anywhere at any time; / from reciting it, one attains liberation; he will certainly become a Sātvata.
First, at the conclusion of the offering of funeral cakes, by Brahmins, the best of the twice-born, / this hymn should be recited; one will obtain inexhaustible [merit from] the ancestral rite.
This is supremely purifying, granting liberation to people; / whoever, having written it down, keeps it in his house with perfect concentration,
his lifespan, prosperity, and strength increase day by day. / If a wise person, having written it down, gives it to a Brahmin at any time,
his ancestors, being liberated, go to the supreme state of Viṣṇu. / And whatever fruit is found in the recitation of the four Vedas,
a man fully obtains by chanting, reciting, and murmuring this hymn. / Having borne the conch, discus, and other [marks], by Brahmins devoted to the Veda,
at the time of ancestral rites, O great goddess, that [rite] certainly becomes inexhaustible. / [Wearing] a garland of lotus seeds on the neck, and bearing the conch, discus, and other [marks],
one should then perform the ancestral rite while reciting and murmuring this hymn / according to the rules, with devotional disposition; it becomes complete, not otherwise."
Therefore, it should be recited diligently by a devoted person. / By reciting it, one obtains everything, and that man prospers in happiness.

6.77.m: Mahādeva said: / I asked the Lord of the Universe about the best of vows among vows, / which causes the increase of sons and grandsons and bestows happiness and good fortune.
I shall narrate it before you; listen now, O beautiful one, / to this divine narrative, the foremost vow of the sages.

A woman who, menstruating, suddenly assumes a sinful state, / is completely freed from great sins solely by performing this vow; / it must be offered to the ancestors for imperishable benefit, accomplishing dharma, desire, and wealth.
Śrī Viṣṇu said: / Formerly there was a mighty-armed brāhmaṇa, master of the Vedas, / constantly devoted to study, a twice-born named Devaśarman.
Engaged in the rites of the sacred fire, always devoted to the six duties, / reverenced among all castes, possessing sons, cattle, and kinsmen.
That foremost brāhmaṇa's wife broke down [with age]; / and when the fifth day arrived in the bright fortnight of the month of Bhādrapada,
Self-controlled and with conquered senses, he performed his father's death-anniversary rite; / at night he invited brāhmaṇas who bestow happiness and good fortune.
When clear dawn arrived, he had other vessels prepared; / he had the cooking done in all the pots by his wife.
Endowed with eighteen flavours, giving delight to the ancestors. / Then, having issued invitations to the brāhmaṇas individually,
All the brāhmaṇas who recite the Vedas arrived at noon. / The best of the twice-born properly offered water for respect, foot-washing, and the rest according to rule.
Defiled by dust during the śrāddha, having washed according to rule, / they all went inside the house and were assigned seats by him.
Food was served by him, especially sweet food; / and the śrāddha was performed according to rule, preceded by the offering of rice-balls.
Betel, sacrificial fees, and various garments— / he gave everything to the twice-born, intently meditating on the ancestors.
All the brāhmaṇas were dismissed, intent on bestowing blessings. / Then, to the clan-members, kinsmen, and other hungry people,
Food was then given by him for their meal according to rule. / At night, while he was seated at the door of his hut,
His brāhmaṇa wife took water and washed his feet. / Just then, a female dog and an ox spoke to each other.
[The female dog said:] / Listen, my beloved, to my words about what the daughter-in-law did; / I will tell you just as it happened, I do not speak falsely.
Once, through the workings of fate, I went into my son's house / to drink the milk that was there; but the daughter-in-law did not see it again.
The milk had been drunk by a serpent, and I saw that; / afterwards it was drunk properly by me, and then the daughter-in-law saw it.
Because of that fault of contact, my hip is constantly broken; / because of that pain, O master, I have become a partaker of misery. / My hip has been broken, and food does not appeal to me at all.
The ox said: / Listen, O bitch, I shall tell you the cause of my distress: / when this very day arrived, the feeding of brāhmaṇas
Was arranged by my son, but no thought was given to me; / neither water nor grass was given anywhere by anyone.
I am indeed without food, a sinner bound here, beset by sin; / by virtue of some particular past sin this has happened, O bitch, without doubt.
That statement, O goddess, was then overheard by the wise son: / 'This is indeed my father directly, born as a beast in my house,
And this is directly my mother, without a doubt; / through the workings of fate she has become a bitch. What can I do with certainty?'
Reflecting thus, that brāhmaṇa obtained no sleep at all; / becoming full of anxiety at night, he remembered the supreme Lord of the Universe:
'I am devoted to various dharmas; how then can good fortune come to me?' / Having reflected thus, he then slept again at night.
When clear dawn arrived, he went before the sages; / in their midst, a warm welcome was extended to him by Vasiṣṭha:
'Speak, O best of brāhmaṇas, the reason for your coming.' / Being questioned thus, the twice-born then made an obeisance:
'Today my birth has borne fruit; today my ritual action has borne fruit; / today my ancestors are satisfied, through the rare sight of you.
The śrāddha was performed as prescribed, and the twice-born were well fed; / likewise, the feeding of all household members was arranged.
After the meal, a female dog arrived there and said: / "In our house there is indeed an ox."
Hear from me the words [she spoke] to that husband, O twice-born: / "The milk pot situated in the house was defiled by a serpent.
It was seen by me, and great anxiety then arose, no doubt: / 'When the food is cooked with this milk,
Then all the brāhmaṇas here will die from eating it.' / Reflecting thus, O master, that milk was then drunk by me.
Then it was seen by the daughter-in-law, and a beating was given to me by her; / because of that I wander around broken; what can I do, utterly wretched?"
Remembering her grief, the bull spoke to the female dog: / "Listen, O bitch, I will tell the cause of my grief:
I was indeed his father directly in a previous birth, O bitch; / today the brāhmaṇas were fed and food was given abundantly,
Yet neither grass nor water was presented before me; / because of that distress, far greater sorrow then arose for me."
Having heard this story, I got no sleep at night; / anxiety arose for me right there, O best of sages.
I am devoted to studying the Vedas, skilled in Vedic rites; / yet great grief has come upon these two. Thinking 'What shall I do?', / I have come to your presence; remove my distress!'
The sage said: / O Ugrajanman, listen to what was done in a previous birth; / this best of the twice-born was indeed in the auspicious city of Kuṇḍana.
And when the fifth day arrived in the month of Bhādrapada, / that vow was not known by him because of his father's śrāddha and other rites.
And she, afflicted by women's course [of menstruation], was the cause of its destruction then, O sinless one; / and all the feeding of the brāhmaṇas was done by her.
It was not known, and was done by that very sinful and wicked woman. / On the first day she is an outcaste woman, on the second a killer of a brāhmaṇa,

On the third she is called a washerwoman, and on the fourth day she becomes pure. / Through that sin, she has become a bitch roaming in her own house; / and this one has become an ox by that action, O you of noble vows.
Ugrajanman said: / A vow, a gift, or a sacrifice, or a holy bath, O you of noble vows— / tell me that by which liberation may especially occur for my parents.
The sage said: / In the month of Bhādrapada, in the bright fortnight, occurs the Ṛṣipañcamī; / for by performing it, the sin caused by menstrual impurity is destroyed.
It bestows sons and grandsons, and gives liberation to the ancestors. / At a river, at a well, at a pond, or in the house of a brāhmaṇa,
One should make a diagram with cow-dung, and place a water-pot right there; / on top of it, one should place a vessel filled with sage-grain.
And a sacred thread, along with gold and fruit; / and the seven Ṛṣis, who grant happiness and good fortune, should be set up.
Having invoked them, they should all be worshipped by those observing the vow. / The offering of food should be wild grains, and the meal also wild grains.
Then the worship of the Ṛṣis should be performed with a single meal a day; / one should worship with supreme devotion, using mantras according to the rule.
An offering of wild grain mixed with ghee, along with a sacrificial gift, should then be given; / it should be given to a brāhmaṇa according to rule, for the satisfaction of the Ṛṣis.
Having listened to the story according to the ordinance and performed circumambulation, / one should offer incense, a lamp, food offering, and water offering separately.
“May the Ṛṣis always make my vow complete; / let them accept the worship offered by me. Homage, homage to the Ṛṣis!
Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, and Prācetasa, / Vasiṣṭha, Marīci, and Atri—accept this water offering! Homage to you!”
In this way the worship should be performed with delightful incenses and lamps. / Liberation of the ancestors arises from the power of this [rite] when performed.
If it is performed due to the ripening of past karma, [or] on account of faults arising from menstrual impurity, / O child, there is liberation for her, without a doubt.
And that vow was performed by him for the purpose of the ancestors' liberation; / devoted to blessings, they departed along the path of liberation.
The sacred Ṛṣipañcamī vow has been proclaimed to the brāhmaṇa. / Those best of men who perform it should be known as partakers in merit.
Those who perform the unexcelled vow of the Ṛṣis, O best of men, / having enjoyed abundant pleasures in this world, go to the abode of Viṣṇu.

6.77.m:
Thus ends the seventy-seventh chapter, entitled 'The Observance of Ṛṣipañcamī,' in the dialogue between Umā's husband and Nārada, in the Uttarakhaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Purāṇa, in the collection of fifty-five thousand [verses].

Seventy-eighth chapter. / Mahādeva said: / Now I shall fully explain the supreme wiping-off of water / just as it was spoken by Pulastya to the noble Dālabhya,

which destroys all diseases and faults and bestows auspiciousness. / I shall declare that to you, O daughter of the mountain; listen!

Śrī Dālabhya said: / O Blessed One, all living beings are afflicted by afflictions such as poison and disease, / overwhelmed by leprosy and planetary spirits, and tormented at all times.

O best of sages, tell me how malevolent sorcery, destructive spirits, / and many terrible diseases do not occur; you ought to speak.

Pulastya said: / Viṣṇu is indeed pleased by those who observe vows, fasts, and rules; / therefore, O best of sages, those men never become afflicted by diseases.

By those who performed neither sacred vow, nor gift, nor penance at that time, / nor pilgrimage, nor worship of deities, nor gave food in abundance,

those people are then to be known as tormented by diseases and faults. / Health, supreme prosperity, whatever one desires in mind—

the servant of Viṣṇu particularly attains all that without doubt. / He incurs neither mental agony nor physical disease, nor bondage caused by poison or planets,

nor fear of the touch of malevolent spirits, once Madhusūdana is pleased. / There is destruction of all faults, and planetary influences are always auspicious;

all diseases are destroyed—truly, truly I say! / Whatever poison is plant-derived, animal-derived, or artificial,

whatever is born of teeth, born of claws, or born in the air, / whatever poison originates from evil spirits and is exceedingly unbearable—

may Janārdana, praised on his behalf, pacify it entirely! / Seizers, ghost-seizers, and other Śākinī-seizers,

the cruel Mukhamaṇḍalikas, Revatī, Vṛddhirevatī, / the fierce seizers called Vṛddhikas, and the Mother-seizers too—

may the deed of child-Viṣṇu slay even child-seizers! / Whatever seizers afflict the elderly, and whatever seizers afflict children,

may they perish at that very moment simply by the sight of Nṛsiṃha! / Nṛsiṃha, frightful to the daityas, with a mouth terrifying with fangs—

having seen him, may all those seizers depart far away in haste! / O glorious Nṛsiṃha, great lion, whose face is brilliant with a garland of flames,

O Lord of all, drive away all his seizers with your gaze! / Whatever diseases, whatever great portents, whatever adversaries, whatever great seizers,

and whatever cruel spirits and dreadful afflictions from seizers there are, / whatever diseases are in weapon wounds, erysipelas and the like,
boils and the rest, and whatever seizers dwell in the limbs— / O protector of the three worlds, repeller of wicked Dānavas,
Sudarśana of great splendor, cut, cut the great fever! / Cut the wind-disease and spider-sore, cut the terrifying great poison,
the severe fatal colic, and the poison-fever along with erysipelas! / — Hāṃ hāṃ hūṃ hūṃ! With your sharp axe strike down the foe!
— Homage to the blessed Sudarśana, whose form tears apart suffering! / And whatever other wicked things torment living beings,
all of them [may Janārdana remove]—Janārdana, the soul of all, the supreme Self; / assuming a certain form, homage to you, O Vāsudeva!
Having hurled the Sudarśana discus, terrifying with wreaths of fire, / pacify all evil, O Acyuta, best of gods!
O great discus Sudarśana, Govinda's excellent weapon, / sharp-edged, of great speed, radiant as ten million suns,
Sudarśana of great blazing, cut, cut, O loud-roaring one! / [Destroy] all sorrows, rākṣasas, and sins, O terrifying one!
Slay misfortune and bestow health, O Sudarśana! / In the east and in the west, and likewise in the south and north,

may Narasiṃha, the soul of the universe, grant protection with his roars! / On the earth, in the atmosphere, and behind, to the sides, and in front, / may the Blessed Janārdana of many forms grant protection!
Just as everything is pervaded by Viṣṇu, along with gods, asuras, and humans, / by that truth, may all his suffering be destroyed!
Just as Viṣṇu is proclaimed the Lord of Yoga among all gods, / by that truth, may all his suffering be destroyed!
Just as Viṣṇu is sung as the supreme Self in the Vedāṅgas, / by that truth, may Keśava, the soul of the universe, bring him happiness!

May there be peace, may there be auspiciousness, and may discomfort vanish! / He has been wiped down by me with kuśa grass originating from Vāsudeva's body.

Cleansed by Govinda—homage to Nārāyaṇa! / Even so, let there be pacification of all sorrows by Hari's word.
Pacified are all your humors, all seizers, poisons, / and spirits are pacified when Madhusūdana is remembered.
This kuśa grass is born of Viṣṇu's body; Janārdana himself is right in front. / All his sorrow has indeed been slain by me; let him become healthy, just as Hari's word decrees!
May there be peace, may there be auspiciousness, and may whatever unhappiness [there is] perish! / Whatever misfortune he has has been cast into the salt ocean.
May he always have health through the praise of Hṛṣīkeśa! / Whatever sin has arrived here from anywhere, let it go back there!
This supreme cleansing rite should be performed in cases of diseases and afflictions / by devotees of Viṣṇu who desire the welfare of living beings.
By this, all sorrows dissolve completely; / this cleansing rite of Viṣṇu is for the complete purification from all sins.
Whether fresh or old, minor or major, such as the slaying of a brāhmaṇa, / all of it is quickly destroyed, just like darkness at the sight of the sun.
Diseases and humors perish, just as small beasts [flee] from a lion; / may seizers, spirits, piśācas, and the rest perish merely from hearing [it]!
It must never be performed for the sake of wealth by those devoted to greed; / when the cleansing rite has been performed, nothing should be accepted, through a desire for [the patient's] welfare.
It should be performed disinterestedly by devotees of Viṣṇu who understand the beginning, middle, and end, / who are always peaceful; otherwise it will bring success.
This is an unequalled accomplishment for men; this is the supreme protection for men. / Indeed, this cleansing rite of Viṣṇu is the supreme medicine.
It was indeed spoken formerly by Brahmā to his son Pulastya; / this sage Pulastya declared it himself to Dālbhya.
For the welfare of all beings, it was revealed by Dālbhya / in the three worlds. Thus is concluded this cleansing rite of Viṣṇu.

It has been told before you, O Goddess, because you are ever devoted to me; / and having heard it all with devotion, one removes diseases and faults.

Thus ends the seventy-eighth chapter, entitled 'The Hymn of Cleansing,' in the dialogue between Umā's husband and Nārada, in the Uttarakhaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Purāṇa, in the collection of fifty-five thousand [verses].

Chapter seventy-nine. Mahādeva said: This divine and exceedingly wondrous cleansing hymn / should especially be recited for the attainment of a son, desire, and wealth.

A wise man should recite this hymn for the attainment of all desired aims. / Those twice-born who recite it once or twice a day,

his lifespan, fortune, and strength increase day by day. / A brāhmaṇa attains knowledge, or a kṣatriya a kingdom;

a vaiśya attains abundance of wealth, and a śūdra attains devotion; / and through others, one attains devotion by reading, hearing, and reciting.

The fruit of the Sāmaveda accrues to him, O daughter of the mountain; / the entire mass of sins is destroyed that very moment.

Knowing this, O goddess, it should be recited by those who are concentrated; / sons indeed and likewise prosperity surely become complete.

6.77.m:
The Vaiṣṇava who, having written it on birch bark, wears it, / having enjoyed happiness in this world, goes to the supreme abode of Viṣṇu.

One who, having recited even a single verse, offers a tulasī [leaf], / all pilgrimages have been made by him once worship of tulasī has been performed.

This supreme Vaiṣṇava hymn bestows liberation; / through its reading, equal to the gift of the earth, one goes to the world of Viṣṇu.

One should repeat this hymn especially out of a desire for the world of Viṣṇu; / for the sake of children's survival, it should be recited by the concentrated.

It brings peace to children afflicted by diseases and seizing spirits; / evil spirits, seizing spirits, and poison are destroyed simply by recitation.

The vipra who recites it wearing a garland made of tulasī upon his neck, / he should indeed be known as a Vaiṣṇava; he goes to the world of Viṣṇu.

The vipra on whose neck a garland is worn, who is marked with conch, discus, and the like, / constantly reciting this hymn, is called a Vaiṣṇava.

Abandoning this world, he goes to the world of Viṣṇu, / freed from delusion and illusion, devoid of hypocrisy and longing.

He should recite this divine hymn; he will attain supreme nirvāṇa. / Blessed on the earth are those vipras who are remembered as Vaiṣṇavas.

Their own soul has indeed been rescued by them, along with their family, no doubt of this. / Most blessed in the world are those devoted to Nārāyaṇa; / devotion must always be practiced by them; they are indeed the Bhagavān's men.
